summary: CIPID adds elements to PIDF that give more contact information about a presentity and its contacts, including references to address book entries and icons. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Adds a little business card with a picture and contact details to someone's online status.

questions: what is the display-name element in pidf
subtitle: Six optional PIDF elements that point a watcher to a presentity's business card, name, homepage, icon, map and sound.

tldr.problem: Basic PIDF presence says little beyond open or closed. Watchers have no standard way to learn more about a presentity or its contacts, such as a card, an icon or a homepage.
tldr.mechanism: CIPID defines six optional elements (card, display-name, homepage, icon, map, sound) that mostly hold URIs and extend the PIDF person element, or less commonly the tuple.
tldr.outcome: Clients can show richer, mostly static contact details. The cost is that fetching those URIs can reveal that a watcher is online. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

facts.label: Elements
facts.value: card, display-name, homepage, icon, map, sound

today: RFC 4482 is a Proposed Standard from July 2006, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. It is designed to be used alongside RFC 4480 and RFC 4481.

sections.title: Where CIPID Fits
sections.content:
CIPID, Contact Information for the Presence Information Data format, extends the XML-based PIDF with basic information that lets a watcher find out more about a presentity or contact. It can be used together with RPID (RFC 4480), the timed-status extension (RFC 4481) and other PIDF extensions.

All elements extend the <person> element or, less commonly, the <tuple> element of the presence data model (RFC 4479). A tuple is extended only when it describes a service that refers to another person, marked by an RPID <relationship> with a value other than self. Every element is optional.

The RFC contrasts the two families: CIPID covers the more static aspects of presence, while RPID covers what changes through the day. That is why CIPID data can often be configured once in a presence client's interface.
sections.eli5: Some of your details change all day, like where you are. CIPID covers the things that stay the same for a long time, like your name and photo.

sections.title: The Six CIPID Elements
sections.content:
Unless noted otherwise, each element may appear at most once.

  • <card>: a URI pointing to a business card, for example in LDIF or vCard format.
  • <display-name>: the name the presentity suggests the watcher's interface show. The watcher may ignore it. Several are allowed only if each has a different xml:lang attribute, for example Latin and Hangul for a Korean-speaking presentity.
  • <homepage>: a URI for general information, typically a web home page.
  • <icon>: a URI for an image to represent the tuple or person. Presentities SHOULD provide sizes and aspect ratios suitable for an icon, and support for JPEG, PNG and GIF is REQUIRED.
  • <map>: a URI for a map, which may be an image, an HTML client-side image map or a GIS document such as GML. Support for PNG and GIF images is REQUIRED.
  • <sound>: a URI for a sound, such as a MIDI or MP3 file. The watcher MAY play it to signal that the presentity became OPEN, and interfaces should let the watcher choose. Support for MP3 (MPEG-2 Layer 3) is RECOMMENDED. It might also show how to pronounce the name.
sections.eli5: There are six blanks to fill in: a business card, a name, a homepage, a picture, a map and a sound. Most of them just hold a web address that leads to the real thing.

sections.title: Example Documents
sections.content:
The RFC gives two examples. The first uses CIPID alone: a PIDF document for pres:someone@example.com whose dm:person holds a card, display name, homepage, icon, map and sound, each in the CIPID namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf:cipid.

The second combines RPID and CIPID. It has a tuple for the presentity's mobile address and another tuple marked with an RPID assistant relationship, which carries its own card and homepage, matching the rule that tuples get CIPID elements only for other people. The dm:person holds the presentity's own card, homepage, icon, map and sound.
sections.eli5: One example is a plain profile. The other shows a person and their assistant, each with their own card and homepage.

sections.title: Schema and IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The schema declares card, homepage, icon, map and sound as xs:anyURI, and display-name as xs:string. The namespace is the URN urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf:cipid.

IANA is asked to register the namespace and the schema under the IETF XML Registry (RFC 3688). The registrant contact is the IETF SIMPLE working group, and the schema registrant is the IESG.
sections.eli5: The format is written down in a precise machine-checkable way and its name is logged on an official list.

sections.title: Internationalization and Language
sections.content:
CIPID delivers only URLs, apart from <display-name>. Resolving a URL can negotiate language and character set within the protocol that URL uses.

Because CIPID is XML, it supports Unicode natively. UTF-8 is RECOMMENDED where parsers disagree about encodings. The xml:lang attribute identifies the language and script of a display name, and if it is missing the default is i-default.
sections.eli5: Names can be written in any alphabet, and a tag says which language each version is in.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The issues are similar to those for RPID (RFC 4480). Watchers need to restrict which content types they render from the icon, homepage, map and sound URIs.

When a watcher fetches these URIs, the presentity may deduce the watcher is currently using the presence application, and could customize the URLs per watcher to see who fetches them. A privacy-conscious client may cache the objects, which can make them stale, but CIPID content is expected to stay the same for days. The URIs could also act as a covert channel, so some organizations may prohibit URLs outside their domain.

For https URIs, the identity check of RFC 2818 section 3.1 must be met. If it fails, the content SHOULD NOT be retrieved and MUST NOT be used.
sections.eli5: When you open a friend's picture link, their server learns you are online. Saving the picture ahead of time hides that. Also, only trust a link if its website is who it claims to be.
